newsitem.title: USA: US Southeast power steady to higher in light trade.
newsitem.headline: US Southeast power steady to higher in light trade.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity values in the southeastern U.S. were steady to slightly higher Thursday in sparse trading, lifted by revised weather forecasts for colder-than-expected temperatures in the Southeast, industry sources said.
"A cold front stalled in Florida. Demand is going to be a little higher tomorrow than they thought," said one power marketer, noting however that activity was very light.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak electricity for Friday delivery was talked in the $22.50-$23.50 a megawatt hour (MWh) range, as compared to Wednesday's $21.00-23.50 trading range.
Firm, off-peak electricity for next-day delivery was also talked higher in the $15.50-16.00 range, but no deals could be confirmed done.
In the northern portion of Tennessee Valley Authority's (TVA) system, firm, peak electricity was assessed steady from Wednesday at $17.00-$18.00, the brokers and marketers said.
However, TVA did not offer its own generation for next-day sale for a fourth day in a row, according to market sources.
Off-peak, firm power in northern TVA for Tuesday delivery was mostly pegged unchanged near $12.00.
A number of nuclear plants will be returning to the grid either late Thursday or early Friday, which may put some downward pressure on hourly prices tomorrow, traders said.
Georgia Power reported its 1,162 megawatt (MW) Vogtle nuclear unit 2 would be back to full production on Friday after tripping off line Wednesday.
Florida Power and Light Co's 666 MW Turkey Point nuclear unit 4 is also scheduled to restart late Thursday or early Friday following Monday's shutdown.
Entergy's 836 MW Arkansas nuclear unit 1 is expected to return to the grid later today.

Separately, Virginia Power also reported that it did yet know when its 911 MW North Anna nuclear unit 1 would restart after tripping off line late Wednesday. The plant's adjacent unit, with a generating capacity of 909 MW, is expected to restart late Thursday.
